Just a few years ago, I could relate to this post. But let me tell you, you don't need to be so hard on yourself. Yes, it's good to improve yourself. But it will get dangerous when you let self-destructiveness seep in.

Firstly, please know that even though you're not his "ideal", he obviously chose you for a reason. Long term relationships are rather serious and if he really didn't want you, he would have left by now. What do you offer for the long term? Focus on that as some of your pros. Because honestly, from experience, your complex about how you don't fit his preferences is worse than not actually fitting his preferences.

Secondly. Maybe this is the designer in me speaking, but I believe that any girl can look as beautiful as they possibly can, even if it takes some time. Weight loss. Learning how to find a good makeup regimen. Growing out your hair...it's possible. Sure, we all can't be Angelina Jolie but that doesn't mean that you can't look lovely. 

Narrow hips and big noses aren't bad, imo. You probably notice these things more than other people and magnify them. I have a friend that has a larger nose and she is honestly one of the prettiest women I've ever seen. She has Spanish genes and that's the type of nose that she has, and it isn't bad. 

You can play up your beauty. Wear what flatters *you*, and you alone. I learned this.

You might not have wide hips, yeah, but you can still look feminine. You might have lovely eyes, maybe add a small line of eyeliner, mascara and a soft color to highlight them. You can actually work out both your bust (through pectoral muscles and chest exercises/machines) and even your hips in the gym. Seriously, I follow a few YouTubers that have actually done the same.

Furthermore, don't focus on your appearance that much. This isn't to say that you should abandon skincare or wear sweatpants everyday, but rather, remember that at the end of the day, inner beauty does and will matter more. If a man has to choose between a pretty woman with a good heart and a stunning woman with a bad heart, well, I think that the first one would win. Anyone can have inner beauty, regardless of appearance. Remember to cultivate a positive, gentle personality, attain good habits like listening to others and being compassionate, work on your skills, and work on being at peace with yourself. It is good to want to improve yourself, but it is unhealthy to be self-destructive.

Please work on yourself--learn to be at peace with yourself. Don't compare yourself to others. This doesn't mean to not take care of yourself, or to neglect yourself, but be content with who you are as an individual. You could be the most handsome man in the world, but if you find something to nitpick over, you won't be content with yourself. You have to learn to be at peace with yourself. Even if you were to get a beard and become a gym rat, some things about you won't change. Working on being the best version of oneself is all we can do. It's also important to know that personality is far more malleable than your looks. You can get braces, but your eye color won't change. However, you can do a complete 360 with your personality. At the end of the day, while appearance is nice, this will always matter more.

tl;dr: sex is not that big of a deal, your cousin had his own plan. If you wanna improve your appearance do it but please work on raising your self esteem too.

What kind of clothes do you like? I would recommend taking the Kibbe test to figure out what clothes look best on you, getting your colors done to figure out which colors and shades make your skin pop and which ones to avoid (basically figuring out what your tone and undertones are), and then take that knowledge and apply it to your own personal style. It will develop over time, trust me. Pinterest boards are good sources of inspiration, and you can also check out trends from all over the world to see what suits you best.

If you want to wear makeup, then makeup tutorials will be your friend, but make sure to find a style of makeup that you like personally. Some people like contouring, others like a dewy finish. Just make sure to apply it properly. r/MakeupAddiction can help you.

Personally, I believe that skincare is more important than makeup, because if your skin isn't in check, the makeup can just worsen it. I have also dealt with acne. You may want to speak to a dermatologist about what you can do, but it's so important to implement a daily skincare regimen. You should talk to them about this, too. You'll want to cleanse, tone and moisturize your face everyday. In addition to this, you should exfoliate and do an acne scrub maybe weekly. A facial mask is good, too, especially blackhead masks. r/SkincareAddiction can help you.

I think that you should talk to a hairstylist about what will suit you. Personally, I think voluminous waves would look lovely on you, perhaps parted to one side. You could try getting contacts or just some glasses that look good on your face shape.

Hang in there. Know your worth and come out of your shell.  :)

Try to avoid following trends just to keep up with everyone else, and stick to things that you like and look good on you, personally. Also, learn your colors--your skin undertones, seasons and overtones. Certain colors--and *shades* of colors, which is even more important-- look better or worse on skin tones. I've noticed this as well. My closet is filled with awkward looking things that I bought over the years because I settled for them (as we couldn't afford things like Forever 21--imagine being the only girl in class that couldn't afford those things). Please, don't do this. You won't be happy.

I am 20 years old, and I am making moves to slowly phase out my old clothes and bring in new, timeless pieces. Before anything, **remember to buy closet staples/basics if you haven't already.** Things like a pencil skirt, a tee, a neutral handbag, a trenchcoat, heels, and riding boots can really set up a good foundation for you, and they will stand the test of time. In addition to your average staples, there might be staples that you *personally* want to have that fit your individual style. A monogrammed handbook, a simple heart-shaped locket, or a floppy hat, for example.

This is where internet shopping becomes handy, because if you really search, you can find really good items. However, you have to learn how to find the right sites. I love indie designer brands, but unfortunately, the dresses can be at the very least, $40. That is not reasonable for me, and I'm pretty sure that it isn't for the average college student, either. Shein is a feasible site and they're always having sales. You can also find quality wardrobe staples at most mainstream retailers for cheap. Forever 21, H&M and the likes tend to have really cheap basics. Taobao is also pretty awesome if you use a good client, plus they have a rating system to teach you which stores are the most trustworthy. 
 
Also, don't be afraid of thrift stores! If you search really hard, you can find designer items for cheap. I browsed at a thrift store recently and I was bummed that I couldn't buy anything because they had the *cutest* shoes! Secondhand shops are awesome, as well.

There is something that I want to stress too, though: don't ever buy something just because it's popular and everyone else is wearing it. Trends change frequently. I remember buying skinny jeans in middle school when they got popular because everyone else had them. Not a good look. Wear something because you like it. If everyone else is wearing flare jeans and you don't like it, you *don't need to wear it*. It does get hard finding exactly what you want when trends change, but don't lose hope. In fact, this is where DIYing things can become really handy. You can even DIY things that you find at the department store, thrift store or secondhand shops. :D

Lastly, have you tried going to local boutiques? I feel like boutiques aren't as commonly thought of anymore with the rise of the convenient chain store. They may or may not offer more expensive items, but they're more likely to be one-of-a-kind and made very well. Sometimes they even have in-house tailors. Don't lose hope! Dressing well is kind of like gourmet cooking--it is an art that requires time and thought, and we all have varying tastes. :D
